faq.q: How do I set up sections and timings?
faq.a: Pick a preset — 3-min Pitch, 5-min Lightning Talk, 10-min Conference, 20-min TED-style, 45-min Lecture, 30-min Viva/Defence or 50-min Classroom — or build your own sections, each with a name, a duration in minutes and optional speaker notes. The total talk time updates as you edit, and your sections are saved in your browser (pt_sections) between visits.

faq.q: What visual and audio cues does it give?
faq.a: A segmented bar shows progress through each section, and the countdown is traffic-light coloured: green when time is comfortable, amber once you're within the warning threshold (set in minutes before the end), and red/over near or past the limit, with the page tinting too. Audio beeps fire at section changes, at the warning point, and at time-up using the Web Audio API — cues still trigger even if a background tab throttled the timer.

faq.q: How accurate is the timer if I switch to my slides?
faq.a: Elapsed time is measured from the wall clock, not by counting ticks, so it stays accurate even when the browser throttles a backgrounded tab — 9 real seconds won't read as 4. Note the tool warns that closing or refreshing the tab loses a running timer. Pause/Resume and Next Section (which jumps to the next section boundary) are available, plus a fullscreen presenter view.

faq.q: Can I review and export my pacing?
faq.a: Yes. Each rehearsal is logged comparing planned total versus actual time and number of sections, so you can see whether runs are converging on your slot. You can export the running order and timings as CSV or download a text plan to keep by the lectern. Keyboard shortcuts: Space pause/resume, N next section, F fullscreen, Esc exit. Everything runs locally in your browser.
